results.raw_content: Using SQuAD v1.1 with five uneven non-IID clients, we conduct a comprehensive comparison across centralized and federated pipelines, with and without RAG, under matched-budget and expanded-budget retrieval settings. To enable fair and controlled comparison, we propose a novel candidate-budget mechanism that explicitly regulates the number of retrieved candidates entering global reranking, thereby decoupling retrieval resource advantages from the learning paradigm. We implement the framework using a Mistral-7B-Instruct generator with LoRA adaptation, and a hybrid retrieval pipeline that integrates BM25 and FAISS-based dense retrieval via reciprocal rank fusion. To enable fair and controlled comparison, we propose a novel candidate-budget mechanism that explicitly regulates the number of retrieved candidates entering global reranking, thereby decoupling retrieval resource advantages from the learning paradigm. [...] Federated learning (FL) provides a privacypreserving alternative to centralized adaptation of large language models (LLMs), but heterogeneous client data and fragmented local corpora can reduce both model robustness and knowledge accessibility at inference time. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) mitigates this limitation by grounding generation in retrieved evidence. However, existing evaluations largely rely on centralized knowledge bases or perform comparisons under mismatched retrieval resources, leading to unfair performance assessment. In this paper, we systematically investigate the integration of FL and RAG for open-domain question answering and, importantly, identify and address a fundamental fairness issue in distributed retrieval evaluation.
